frequency_question: What proportion of major legislative proposals complete the full Senate passage pipeline (committee action to final roll call vote) within a single 300-day legislative operating window?
membership_rule: Members: Federal statutory bills introduced in the Senate or received from the House that underwent committee referral and reached a final floor vote in the Senate. Excluded: Non-binding resolutions, unanimous consent routine administrative measures, and bills that died entirely without committee action or floor scheduling.

cases.name: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024
National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025

provenance_note: 5 cases named, 12 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (2.4x)
coverage_note: 5 named major benchmark items representing primary legislative vehicle completions out of roughly 12 major contested efforts in recent congressional terms.
known_gaps: Excludes minor technical corrections bills and purely symbolic measures that bypass standard procedural friction timelines.
skeleton: Major legislative vehicles processed per 2-year Congress divided by total major proposed vehicles introduced that reach committee stage, multiplied by the temporal completion rate within 300 active calendar days.
multiplier: 5 major enacted packages per standard high-priority legislative track divided by roughly 12 major contested partisan priorities attempted per Congress, yielding a base procedural completion success rate of approximately 42 percent under assumed full cooperation.
validity_reason: The structural rules of the U.S. Senate (such as committee timelines and floor scheduling mechanics) remain stable across congressional terms until a new Senate changes its standing rules.
